rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A useful metaphor conveys an additional meaning through an underlying simile; its possible forms are too numerous for exhaustive treatment here.
rows.anchor: وجملة تلك الفائدة وذلك الغرض التشبيه إلا أن طرقه تختلف حتى تفوت النهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a brave man a lion intensifies the description and places the lion’s force, daring, and ferocity before the listener.
rows.anchor: المبالغة في وصف المقصود بالشجاعة وإيقاعك منه في نفس السامع صورة الأسد في بطشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling someone a sea suggests generosity and openhandedness; sun and moon suggest beauty, radiance, and brilliance.
rows.anchor: وهكذا أفدت باستعارة البحر سعته في الجود وفيض الكف وبالشمس والبدر ما لهما من الجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a man a drawn sword can mean that he is forceful in supporting you or that his judgment is penetrating.
rows.anchor: وسللت سيفا على العدو تريد رجلا ماضيا في نصرتك أو رأيا نافذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a human by the horse-specific al-mirsan adds no sense beyond saying nose, so this is not a meaningful metaphor; useful metaphorical simile is shared across languages.
rows.anchor: اختصاص المرسن بغير الآدمي لا يفيد أكثر مما يفيده الأنف في الآدمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the finest poetry is truthful may mean poetry offering sound wisdom, moral counsel, and distinctions between good and bad conduct.
rows.anchor: خير الشعر ما دل على حكمة يقبلها العقل وأدب يجب به الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truthful praise can mean praising men only for qualities they actually possess, as the source says Zuhayr did.
rows.anchor: كما قيل كان زهير لا يمدح الرجل إلا بما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposing view calls the best poetry the most untrue: poetic craft expands through imaginative claims, figurative extension, and exaggeration in praise, blame, and description.
rows.anchor: ومن قال اكذبه ذهب إلى أن الصنعة إنما يمد باعها وينشر شعاعها ويتسع ميدانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers truthful poetry: its sound reasoning, durable effect, clearer benefit, and richer yield outweigh the wider invention available to imaginative poetry.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لأنهما قولان يتعارضان في اختيار نوعى الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason and verification ultimately support the truthful kind of poetry, even though imaginative poetry offers a wider field for invention.
rows.anchor: والعقل بعد على تفضيل القبيل الأول وتقديمه وتفخيم قدره وتعظيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that merit rests on piety rather than inherited rank is a sound rational meaning shared by people across generations; the Qur’an gives its finest expression.
rows.anchor: وأعلى مناسبة وأنورها وأجلها وأفخرها قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that a person whose deeds hold him back will not be advanced by his lineage.
rows.anchor: وقول النبي من أبطأ به عمله لم يسرع به نسبه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells the Banu Hashim that people will come to him with deeds, while they must not come relying on lineage.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام يا بني هاشم لا تجيئني الناس بالأعمال وتجيئوني بالأنساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without acquired virtues and notable deeds, an ancestor would have no earned distinction for descendants to invoke in a comparison of merit.
rows.anchor: لما كان أولا ولكان العلم من أمره مجهلا ولما تصور افتخار الثاني بالانتماء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying that all descend from Adam, who was made from dust, further undercuts inherited descent as a basis for superiority.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال كلكم لآدم وآدم من التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic maxim says inherited standing counts only when matched by merit a person acquires for himself.
rows.anchor: وما الحسب الموروث لا دردره بمحتسب إلا بآخر مكتسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One image, a flint striking sparks, can branch into several comparisons: a generous person, a keen mind, success, and attaining one’s aim.
rows.anchor: الزند بإيرائه يعطيك شبه الجواد والذكى الفطن وشبه النجح في الأمور والظفر بالمراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A flint that fails to spark can suggest a miser, a dull person whose mind yields nothing, or someone whose effort comes to nothing.
rows.anchor: وبأصلاده شبه البخيل الذي لا يعطيك شيئا والبليد الذي لا يكون له خاطر ينتج فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon can suggest a person’s fame, distinction, honor, and elevation, as well as completion after deficiency and decline after fullness.
rows.anchor: ويعطيك من القمر الشهرة في الرجل والنباهة والعز والرفعة ويعطيك الكمال عن النقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Tammam uses the growing crescent to picture a noble child developing until he resembles his distinguished origin in merit and intellect.
rows.anchor: إن الهلال إذا رأيت نموه أيقنت أن سيصير بدرا كاملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Buhturi compares a rise from one rank of honor to a higher one with a crescent gradually becoming full.
rows.anchor: مثل الهلال بدا فلم يبرح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet compares a person’s life to the moon: growth reaches fullness, then old age brings decline and disappearance.
rows.anchor: المرء مثل هلال حين تبصره يبدو ضئيلا ضعيفا ثم يتسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Babak likens a minister’s partial share in royal authority to the moon midway through its growth; the verse praised Abu Ali after Fakhr al-Dawla appointed him vizier.
rows.anchor: وأعرت شطر الملك شطر كماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Khwarizmi’s couplet contrasts a host’s long stays when wealthy with his brief visits when poor.
rows.anchor: أراك إذا أيسرت خيمت عندنا مقيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech gives knowledge its ranks, reveals its forms and inner meanings, and allows its fruits to be shared; the opening of al-Rahman illustrates this divine teaching.
rows.anchor: الكلام هو الذي يعطي العلوم منازلها ويبين مراتبها ويكشف عن صورها ويجني صنوف ثمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguishes humans from other animals through speech, which the author presents as a great divine favor.
rows.anchor: وبه أبان الله تعالى الإنسان من سائر الحيوان ونبه فيه على عظم الامتنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without speech, knowledge and thought would remain trapped within their possessors, and people could not distinguish faith from unbelief or praise from blame.
rows.anchor: ولبقيت القلوب مقفلة على ودائعها والمعاني مسجونة في مواضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech’s special function is to present what is known with the qualities and states that knowledge has found in it.
rows.anchor: أنه يريك المعلومات بأوصافها التي وجدها العلم عليها ويقرر كيفياتها التي تناولها المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best speech most fully realizes this distinctive function; excellence does not lie in isolated words but in their particular composition and order.
rows.anchor: والألفاظ لا تفيد حتى تؤلف ضربا خاصا من التأليف ويعمد بها إلى وجه دون وجه من التركيب والترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a camel shepherd’s staff weak or firm can serve the same end, good care: weakness suggests gentleness, while firmness suggests effective control without repeated blows.
rows.anchor: فإنهما يرجعان إلى غرض واحد وهو حسن الرعية والعمل بما يصلحها ويحسن أثره عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘weak staff’ means the shepherd is gentle and chooses a soft stick rather than hurting the animals needlessly.
rows.anchor: أنه رفيق بها مشفق عليها لا يقصد من حمل العصا أن يوجعها بالضرب من غير فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘firm staff’ means the shepherd knows how to manage the herd, steer it from harmful pasture, and keep it together through disciplined leadership.
rows.anchor: أنه جيد الضبط لها عارف بسياستها في الرعي يزجرها عن المراعى التي لا تحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A different line calling someone firm of staff and aloof from flirtation does not make the same point as the shepherding examples.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر صلب العصا جاف عن التغزل فهذا لم يبين ما بينه الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘A finger’ can indicate a shepherd’s skillful effect because delicate work depends on precise movement of the fingers; it is not a general independent word for an effect.
rows.anchor: فدلوا عليه بالأصبع لأن الأعمال الدقيقة لها اختصاص بالأصابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary usage confirms the link: people do not call traces of a house ‘its fingers’ or describe an effect generically as a good or bad finger.
rows.anchor: لا يقولون رأيت أصابع الدار بمعنى آثار الدار وله أصبع حسنة وأصبع قبيحة

words: بلى قادرين على أن نسوى بنانه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the restoration of fingertips as the power to make them like a camel’s hoof, disabling delicate work and showing what fingers enable.
rows.anchor: أي نجعلها كخف البعير فلا تتمكن من الأعمال اللطيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same principle applies to ‘hand’ when it signifies a benefaction through the hand’s characteristic action; a bare phrase such as ‘acquired a blessing’ carries no such image.
rows.anchor: كذلك ينبغي أن تعلم ذلك في اليد لقيام هذه العلة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives proverbs, poetry, and explicit simile as examples of figurative representation, including the comparison of the addressee to night.
rows.anchor: وقوله السفر ميزان القوم وقول الأعرابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers who stop at a shared general label miss important distinctions; fine inquiry is needed to see where cases meet and where they diverge.
rows.anchor: الأمور التي تلتقي عند الجملة وتتباين لدى التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The natural order is to discuss literal and figurative usage, then simile and representation, then metaphor: metaphor is broader, and simile is its basis.
rows.anchor: أن المجاز أعم من الاستعارة والواجب في قضايا المراتب أن نبدأ بالعام قبل الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite that logical order, the author begins with metaphor because circumstances call for it, then promises to return to the other topics and complete the discussion.
rows.anchor: إلا أن ههنا أمورا اقتضت أن تقع البداية بالاستعارة وبيان صدر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First impressions come through the senses and natural disposition before reasoning, so they are more intimate and familiar to the soul.
rows.anchor: العلم الأول آتى النفس أولا من طريق الحواس والطباع ثم من جهة النظر والرويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A simile makes an abstract meaning familiar by translating it from pure thought into something sensed or naturally known, like introducing a stranger through a beloved friend or unveiling a hidden object.
rows.anchor: فأنت إذن مع الشاعر وغير الشاعر إذا وقع المعنى في نفسك غير ممثل ثم مثله كمن يخبر عن شىء من وراء حجاب ثم يكشف عنه الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Representation can support a strange, disputed claim: the poet says an exceptional person surpasses humanity as musk, though part of deer blood, has left the nature and qualities of blood.
rows.anchor: فإن تفق الأنام وأنت منهم فإن المسك بعض دم الغزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘making the earth’s delight life,’ the metaphor lies in the noun ‘life’ itself; it need not be attributed to the earth as a real life it possesses through another source.
rows.anchor: اثبت بهجة الأرض حياة أو جعلها حياة أفلا ترى المجاز قد ظهر لك في الحياة من غير أن أضفتها إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexical metaphor assigns a word a different but intelligible meaning, as when ‘life’ is used for knowledge; the transferred name still conveys a rational quality.
rows.anchor: فنحن إذا تجوزنا في الحياة فأردنا بها العلم فقد أودعنا الاسم معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘spring made the flowers,’ the verb is not transferred to a new intelligible sense; spring is only imagined as causing what appears with it, so this is an attribution of agency, not a lexical metaphor.
rows.anchor: لما كان النور لا يوجد إلا بوجود الربيع توهم للربيع تأثير في وجوده فاثبت له ذلك اثبات الحكم أو الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited lines picture distinguished men whose standing opens kings’ gates for them, while mere approach does not guarantee entry.
rows.anchor: ليس كل من دنا من أبواب الملوك فتحت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal complexity is blameworthy when words are ordered so that the intended meaning is not clear and the listener must find it by an indirect route.
rows.anchor: وأما التعقيد فإنما كان مذموما لأجل أن اللفظ لم يرتب الترتيب الذي يمثله تحصل الدلالة على الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effort can make discovery more pleasurable when the meaning merits it, but exhausting labor for a poor result has the opposite effect.
rows.anchor: فرحا بالمعنى وأنسا به وسرورا بالوقوف عليه إذا كان لذلك أهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst complexity tires without benefit and resembles a miser who keeps someone hoping with promises, then offers nothing worth the effort.
rows.anchor: أحق أصناف التعقيد بالذم ما يتعبك ثم لا يجدي عليك ويؤرقك ثم لا يروق لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author faults Abu Tammam for strained diction and constructions so obscure that grammar cannot readily repair them.
rows.anchor: مثل ما تجده لأبى تمام من تعسفه في اللفظ وذهابه به في نحو من التركيب لا يهتدى النحو إلى إصلاحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Tammam’s line about a ‘second’ in the middle of the sky and two men having no second in the cave exemplifies this contrived arrangement.
rows.anchor: يعمي الإعراب في طريقه ويصل في تعريفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rummah’s silver touched by gold image is more readily possible, while pearls scattered on blue cloth are rarer and therefore more novel.
rows.anchor: كأنها فضة قد مسها ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Composite similes divide into images that cannot occur, such as ruby banners on emerald spears, and images that can occur but are rare, such as pearls on blue cloth.
rows.anchor: المقدر الذي لا يباشر الوجود نحو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Impossible imagined images create greater wonder than rare possible ones because nothing is farther from sight than what cannot exist; aesthetic force rises with the strength of this cause.
rows.anchor: لا مزيد في بعد الشىء عن العيون على أن يكون وجوده ممتنعا أصلا حتى لا يتصور إلا في الوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This distinction explains why similes differ in strangeness and delight, and why some produce a stronger thrill than others.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التقرير ما تعلم به الطريق إلى التشبيه من أين تفاوت في كونه غريبا
